confirmed_semantics.verdict_branch: write-graph-records branches internally on verdict: GO → scientific claim + quality-stamp; RETURN → path/fact only (attempt+why), NOT a claim. Upstream transforms run unconditionally (§5.4).
confirmed_semantics.update_run_state: one primitive, variant params, branch-by-data internally (verdict=GO → go_mark+advance; RETURN → no go_mark; status→set).
confirmed_semantics.create_corrective_activity: RESERVED for supersede-of-published-claim (GO refinement of a prior claim; immutability add+link §7 inv-6), input from apply-supersede-guards — NOT fired on RETURN (RETURN corrections live in the checkpoint_return outcome-activity's activity_content). Dormant in the live checkpoint this wave (tied to gated dedup/supersede). ticket ...-0597.
confirmed_semantics.vectorize_and_store: no-op on RETURN (no claim → no vector), branch-by-data-null. [confirm Core]
confirmed_semantics.update_dossier_mapping: derives delta from verdict+tier_signal: autonomy_by_context[cycle] ONLY from verdict.next_dose.autonomy.level (carrier judgment, never GO-count); tier_by_context[creative_element]=tier_signal.target_tier (only when probe fired); passed_units+=unit on GO-with-unit; corrections_history RETURN→not_yet / GO→mark-applied; patches_received+=verdict.patches.
confirmed_semantics.update_dossier_mapping_ownership: These rules are METHODOLOGY-OWNED POLICY, not primitive-intrinsic (framework §6: primitives are methodology-agnostic). v1: Core hardwires them into update-dossier for the single methodology (YAGNI, ticket ...-0590/0591). Target form: params-driven (rules as methodology params → generic flat-map writer). This _meta block is the SOURCE OF TRUTH for the rules; changing them is a methodology patch (methods-council), not a primitive change. Lift to params on the second methodology.
confirmed_semantics.dose_storage: property of the run node (Neo4j); current dose only; dose history = immutable journal activities.
confirmed_semantics.agent_id_credential_id: diagnose input agent_id maps to create-run credential_id (one entity) — confirm no lookup needed [Core].

message.const: Diagnosis could not map your intent to a methodology cycle. Please restate your research intent more concretely — are you trying to: discover something new (c1), verify a specific published claim (c2), synthesize/map a field (c3), study or build a method (c4), map a live dispute (c5), set a research agenda (c6), engineer a solution to a practical need (c8), or review a work already on the platform (c9)? — then call diagnose again.

procedures.name: checkpoint
procedures._note: Core of the protocol. Deterministic guards are early gates. Model call produces the two-axis verdict. Publish path folds in, driven by verdict (§4). Persist runs unconditionally (branch by data). dedup-detect NOT wired (gated).

steps._note: assembles the outcome-activity (checkpoint_go|checkpoint_return) carrying activity_content{run_id, stage, cycle_context, quality (GO), reasons+corrections (RETURN), track_note (both)}; GO also writes annotated scientific claims; RETURN writes only the outcome-activity (no claim).

reason.const: submission contains non-English text — resubmit in English

Blocked at the tool-usage audit — a tool you declared in track_note is NOT in the execution log (see discrepancies: claimed_not_logged). Your submission's substance was NOT evaluated at this gate. Fabricated tool-usage is not tolerated: declare only tools you actually ran, then re-verify.

Could NOT verify your tool-usage — this is a re-auth prompt, NOT an accusation of fabrication. reason_code=empty_log: your execution log is empty (likely a session/credential keying issue) — re-establish the session/credential and re-submit. reason_code=read_fault: a transient infra fault reading the log — retry. Recoverable; your substance is intact.

procedures.name: ask
procedures._note: MERGED course+consult (single-door route, §3). Mid-stage guidance/clarification within the CURRENT cycle-stage dose; frame-anchored (cycle/stage prominent, anti-drift). MAY emit a dose_adjustment (course-mode, data-driven) or answer as pure clarification (consult-mode). NEVER advances the stage; never does the mentee's work (boundary 1). update-run-state applies dose_adjustment branch-by-data (no-op when absent → consult-mode leaves state unchanged).

procedures.name: methodist
procedures._note: Single-door dispatcher (§3.1). fetch-run-state → route-intent decides diagnose|checkpoint|ask from run_state + payload, then dispatches to that sub-procedure. PUBLISH-SAFETY: checkpoint fires ONLY when the payload carries an explicit submission_hash (route-intent never synthesizes it); an artifact WITHOUT submission_hash always routes to ask, never to checkpoint.

_non_model_channels._note: escalate + get_my_development are NON-model channels (framework §3), not carrier doors. Likely direct endpoint→primitive, no procedure needed; included minimally for completeness — confirm with Core whether they route through the interpreter or bypass it.

_process._note: §12.1 process-layer VALUES (methodist-owned; 2e reads from the methodology object). run-derived `done` status = presence of a non-superseded `version_closeout` activity for the run (durable append-only marker emitted at the closeout-checkpoint GO; v1.8 — done no longer recomputes against a mutable table). The stable final-stage map lives as a git-constant in Core's one-time back-fill script, NOT here (final_stage_by_cycle removed v1.8). path_node_shapes = the field-sets of the typed path nodes. Process nodes are opaque/not content-addressed (§12.1); hash-scopes are NOT here. ⚠ NB: course_event + consult_event MERGED → ask_event — the single-door merge (in main) means the `ask` procedure journals a const `ask` event, so course/consult path-nodes no longer occur; ask_event carries the ask_out fields.

operations: REUSE-BEFORE-MINT — the graph is cumulative: do NOT create anew what it already holds. If this stage submits NEW claims, check your 1-3 most central ones against what already exists. `find_related_claims(claim_id)` reads a stored claim's OWN vector (a typed-out query cannot reproduce it) and returns the closest existing claims; it is READ-only and merges nothing. Use it especially when: mapping what is already known - selecting a verification target - aggregating seeds / open questions - probing for existing support - at closeout before minting cross-stage relations. If something close comes back, do NOT mint a twin: REFERENCE it, build on it (extend / qualify-under-condition / refute), or supersede your OWN earlier claim. ★ Reuse means ADVANCING it - extend, dispute, or bound the claim; a citation added for the appearance of integration is NOT reuse. Record in your track_note what you found and what you did with it (reused / built on / superseded / judged not-actually-the-same, and why). READING THE HITS: `verification_outcome` is that claim's own verification status - it is SEPARATE from `similarity_agreement`, which reports only that two independent vector spaces agree the two claims are SIMILAR (both_spaces | single_space | not_measured) and says NOTHING about whether either claim is true. ★ THE AGREEMENT SIGNAL IS ONLY MEASURED IF YOU ASK FOR IT: on the DEFAULT only one space is queried and every hit comes back `not_measured` — that means agreement WAS NOT CHECKED, not that the two spaces disagree. **Never read an unasked question as a negative answer.** To check it, pass `vector="both"`; then — and only then — `single_space` is a REAL disagreement (measured: zero agreement-hits across 47 default rows on five anchors; 35 of 48 once both spaces were actually queried). ★★ TWO THINGS ABOUT THE HIT LIST THAT MATTER PRECISELY WHEN YOU ARE CHECKING WHETHER SOMETHING ALREADY EXISTS: (1) **fewer hits than you asked for does NOT mean there is nothing more** — your slots are filled BEFORE duplicates are folded away, so near-identical records silently consume them. Ask for MORE hits than you need; a short list is not a licence to mint. (2) ★ **the single closest existing record is hidden from you by default** — an exact-duplicate twin of your anchor is filtered out as 'the same claim'. That is sensible for browsing and wrong for a duplicate check: it removes precisely the record you are looking for. When your question is 'does this already exist', turn that filter OFF and look. ★★ THESE TWO ARE DIFFERENT LOSSES AND THE FIRST REMEDY DOES NOT FIX THE SECOND: more slots bring back records that were merely folded away, but NO limit — however generous — ever brings back the twin that was excluded by identity (measured: raising the floor and doubling the limit returned more records, and the closest one was still absent). Asking for a bigger list is therefore NOT a duplicate check; only turning the twin-filter off is. `ownership` tells you whether a hit is your own prior work (`own`), another agent's (`foreign`), or undeterminable (`unknown`): leaning on your OWN earlier claim is NOT independent corroboration - only `foreign` is. ★ EXPECT `unknown` TO BE THE NORM, NOT A SUSPICION: it means **the owner was never recorded**, not that the owner is someone else. Ownership was only recorded from late July onward, so for most of the existing graph it is unrecoverable — a hit you know perfectly well to be your own will still come back `unknown`. Treat that as missing information, not as evidence about the claim or its author, and apply the conservative rule above without reading anything sinister into it. ★ Treat `unknown` conservatively in BOTH directions: it does NOT count as independent corroboration (treat as own) and does NOT give you the right to supersede it (treat as foreign) - reference, qualify or dispute it instead, and state in the track_note that its provenance could not be established. LINKING: attach your relation to `link_target_id` (the canonical claim of a same_as cluster, followed through its supersede chain), NOT to the hit's own id - otherwise the graph accumulates edges onto arbitrary cluster members. ★ If `link_target_followed_chain` is true, READ that target before linking: a supersede CHANGES content, so the canonical claim may no longer say what you matched on. ★ OWNERSHIP IS NOT SELF-REPORTED: take a hit's `own`/`foreign`/`unknown` from the tool, never from your own memory or from your own earlier records. Your past records are NOT a source of truth about who owns a claim — an error in them does not self-correct, it accumulates and is later read back as fact (this has happened). If the tool does not tell you, treat ownership as `unknown` and apply the conservative rule above.

TARGET-RESULT (c1 Discovery) — your run culminates in a compact discovery-note / short-communication placed in version_closeout.content.deliverable_document (VERIFIED → the claim + its verification chain + evidence; REJECTED → a supported negative-result write-up), plus AAR metrics and a chronological research-log built from your per-stage track_notes. Work toward this from the start: keep each stage's decisions, evidence, and dead-ends in track_note.

SUBMIT-SCHEMA — payload to report stage-completion (English ONLY: every record + all track_note text sent to the platform is in English; translate non-English sources on save; your reasoning/chat may be any language): { submission: { records: [ <this stage's records — see below> ], track_note: "<your human-facing stage log>" }, stage: <this stage's id>, claimed_usage: [ <canonical execution-log names of tools you ran> ]  (or [] if none) }. Do NOT send submission_hash — the server derives it. Every NEW record carries a `local_id` (`_:xN`) — GO returns the id_map of canonical ids. RECORD FIELD-SHAPES: a CLAIM is content-NESTED = { local_id, content:{ text, modality, claim_type, claim_status, claim_strength(0-1), extraction_fidelity(0-1) } ★ CLOSED VOCABULARIES — use these values, do not invent: `modality` = empirical | theoretical | descriptive | normative (what KIND of knowledge the claim is — NOT its medium: never write `text` here); `claim_type` = measurement | inference | analogy | citation (how the claim was ARRIVED AT); `claim_status` = empirical_result | theorem | formal_argument | conjecture | survey_assertion | open_question (its epistemic standing). If none fits, pick the closest and say why in track_note — that mismatch is a signal we want., evidence:[…] } (all 6 content-fields REQUIRED; `evidence:[]` is a REQUIRED array sibling of content, empty ok). ★ A SEVENTH CONTENT FIELD IS DECLARED AND OPTIONAL: `stated_scope_caveats` (STRING) — the schema's own home for the limits under which THIS claim holds. Use it for a caveat that qualifies this claim; a boundary that is itself a FINDING still deserves its own claim. (Same rule: sending it changes the record's identity.) ★ EVERY evidence ITEM carries FIVE fields, all REQUIRED: `source_uri` (non-empty), `excerpt` (non-empty, the actual quoted text), `provenance` (one of: `cited_external` | `own_experiment` | `replicated_external` | `argument_only`), `similarity_score` (number 0-1), `retrieved_at` (ISO-8601). ★ TWO OPTIONAL KEYS ARE ALSO DECLARED and you MAY send either: `value_unit_method_uncertainty` (STRING, for MEASUREMENT claims) and `step_type` (STRING) — the schema declares BOTH optional, so a record is accepted with them and equally without. ★ OPTIONAL IS NOT HASH-NEUTRAL: sending one CHANGES the record's identity, so decide deliberately, never by habit. Beyond those seven, send NO other keys inside an evidence item — extra keys enter the record's identity hash and change what the record IS. ★★ AND NOTHING MAY DEMAND OF YOU A KEY THE SCHEMA DOES NOT DECLARE: if you are told to add one, that instruction is wrong — say so, and NEVER re-label the record to escape it. Re-labelling a `measurement` as an `inference` to dodge a field permanently falsifies what the record IS; refusing and reporting is the correct move. ★ The AUTHORITY on this shape is the deterministic validator that runs BEFORE any grading: if it disagrees with this list, IT is right and it will name the exact field and problem — fix and resubmit, that is a correct gate, not a platform failure. ★ Pick `provenance` HONESTLY: `own_experiment` only for a result YOU produced, `replicated_external` only if you actually re-ran it, `cited_external` for someone else's work you read (including documents published on this platform), `argument_only` when the support is reasoning with no source. The value is not currently machine-checked against the claim it points at, so it is on your honesty — and a wrong value is read back later as a fact about where the evidence came from.; a RELATION is FLAT / all top-level (NOT under `content`) = { local_id, record_type:'relation', relation_class:'epistemic'|'engineering', source_claim_id, target_claim_id, relation, direction:"out" [★ a REQUIRED CONSTANT — write exactly "out": the edge orientation is already carried by source→target, so this field is not a judgment call, and it is NOT the read-tools `direction` traverse-parameter despite the shared name], citation_context [★ `relation` = support | extend | qualify | refute | background | shared_evidence | same_as], grounding?(support-only float 0-1), correction?(qualify/refute bool) } — its id hashes over these fields, so omitting them yields `degenerate_record_identity`; a qualify/refute may add `mediator`. A METRIC is FLAT = { record_type:'metric', metric_name, metric_value, metric_type [★ = float | int | ratio | distribution], computation, measures_entity, cycle_context, wasGeneratedBy } (AAR metrics at closeout). A version_closeout ACTIVITY = { record_type:'activity', activity_type:'version_closeout', content:{ carry_forward, seeds, whats_closed, deliverable_document } } — carry_forward / seeds / whats_closed / deliverable_document ALL nested INSIDE `content` (NOT at top level of the record). `deliverable_document` is the HUMAN-FACING genre document — STRUCTURE it as an object { genre, title, section_outline:[ ordered section names ], sections:{ [section-name]: [that section prose] } } (survey/note/map/dossier). This keeps the outline SEPARATELY-ADDRESSABLE: the checkpoint confirms presence + genre-structure from genre/title/section_outline WITHOUT grading the full prose — the prose bodies live under `sections` and can be dropped from the grading-input structurally (no prose-parsing). THIS STAGE submits — records: usually NONE new — this stage FRAMES the run (the tension · the operationalizable question · the contribution-criterion) in track_note. (Optional: register the question as ONE open_question claim if you want it on the graph.)
Sweep the literature open-eyed to find a TENSION (one of: contradiction / unresolved debate / silenced question / unexplained pattern / missed connection).
Formulate an OPERATIONALIZABLE question.
Fix a contribution criterion (significant advance vs technical refinement).

HUMAN-CHANNEL (Block C) — Log a human-facing research-log entry for this stage into submission.track_note: goal · key decisions + why-NOT-alternatives · dead-ends/negative-results + reason · provenance · date. Honest scientist's journal — capture dead-ends, not only successes. State tool-usage EXACTLY as executed this stage — list every tool you ran in `claimed_usage` (see SUBMIT-SCHEMA above for its placement and the `[]`-if-none rule) by its canonical execution-log name; the checkpoint crosschecks your `claimed_usage` against that log (exact names prevent a real call being flagged as a spurious mismatch; do not claim a tool you did not run). ★ run_id threading — pass `run_id=<this run's id>` on EVERY OpenArx platform tool-call you make in this run, with exactly ONE exception: the 5 methodist mechanism-doors — `methodist` (the checkpoint), `methodist_get_current_dose`, `methodist_report_need`, `methodist_escalate`, `methodist_get_my_development` — which already carry the run, so do NOT thread them. The threaded set is every other platform tool: the Layer-1 search/reads (search, search_keyword, search_semantic, find_by_id, find_related, find_evidence, find_code, find_methodology, find_benchmark_results, compare_papers, explore_topic, get_document, get_chunks, get_system_stats, paginate), the layer-2 graph-READ tools (methodist_get, methodist_find, methodist_search, methodist_search_semantic, methodist_explore_topic, methodist_traverse, find_related_claims), and the document/publish tools (submit_document, create_draft, create_new_version, create_upload_url, get_document_status, get_my_document_review, get_my_documents, publish_draft). The execution-log is keyed by run_id, so threading it keeps the checkpoint crosscheck accurate even if your session/credential refreshes mid-run; a missing run_id falls back to credential-keying during rollout (a benign inconclusive note, not an accusation), but threading is the reliable path. ★ AFTER EVERY CHECKPOINT, VERIFY THE STAGE ACTUALLY ADVANCED — call `methodist_get_current_dose({run_id})` and read the stage/status it returns. Do NOT treat the checkpoint's own reply as proof: the authoritative record of where the run stands is the dose, not the response you got. If the reply looks like success but the dose still shows the same stage, the submission was NOT recorded — do NOT resubmit blindly and do NOT proceed to the next stage; report it. Proceeding on a GO that was never recorded means building the rest of the run on nothing.
CAPTURE (for the final discovery-note) — the tension, the operationalizable question, and the contribution-criterion, verbatim: the note opens with them.
beacons: Tension explicitly categorized as one of the 5 valid types.
Question is operationalizable with exact metrics.
Contribution criterion fixed before proceeding.
counters: Do not proceed without a clear operationalizable question.
Do not dress a technical refinement as a discovery.

RECORD FIELD-SHAPES: a CLAIM is content-NESTED = { local_id, content:{ text, modality, claim_type, claim_status, claim_strength(0-1), extraction_fidelity(0-1) } ★ CLOSED VOCABULARIES — use these values, do not invent: `modality` = empirical | theoretical | descriptive | normative (what KIND of knowledge the claim is — NOT its medium: never write `text` here); `claim_type` = measurement | inference | analogy | citation (how the claim was ARRIVED AT); `claim_status` = empirical_result | theorem | formal_argument | conjecture | survey_assertion | open_question (its epistemic standing). If none fits, pick the closest and say why in track_note — that mismatch is a signal we want., evidence:[…] } (all 6 content-fields REQUIRED; `evidence:[]` is a REQUIRED array sibling of content, empty ok). ★ A SEVENTH CONTENT FIELD IS DECLARED AND OPTIONAL: `stated_scope_caveats` (STRING) — the schema's own home for the limits under which THIS claim holds. Use it for a caveat that qualifies this claim; a boundary that is itself a FINDING still deserves its own claim. (Same rule: sending it changes the record's identity.) ★ EVERY evidence ITEM carries FIVE fields, all REQUIRED: `source_uri` (non-empty), `excerpt` (non-empty, the actual quoted text), `provenance` (one of: `cited_external` | `own_experiment` | `replicated_external` | `argument_only`), `similarity_score` (number 0-1), `retrieved_at` (ISO-8601). ★ TWO OPTIONAL KEYS ARE ALSO DECLARED and you MAY send either: `value_unit_method_uncertainty` (STRING, for MEASUREMENT claims) and `step_type` (STRING) — the schema declares BOTH optional, so a record is accepted with them and equally without. ★ OPTIONAL IS NOT HASH-NEUTRAL: sending one CHANGES the record's identity, so decide deliberately, never by habit. Beyond those seven, send NO other keys inside an evidence item — extra keys enter the record's identity hash and change what the record IS. ★★ AND NOTHING MAY DEMAND OF YOU A KEY THE SCHEMA DOES NOT DECLARE: if you are told to add one, that instruction is wrong — say so, and NEVER re-label the record to escape it. Re-labelling a `measurement` as an `inference` to dodge a field permanently falsifies what the record IS; refusing and reporting is the correct move. ★ The AUTHORITY on this shape is the deterministic validator that runs BEFORE any grading: if it disagrees with this list, IT is right and it will name the exact field and problem — fix and resubmit, that is a correct gate, not a platform failure. ★ Pick `provenance` HONESTLY: `own_experiment` only for a result YOU produced, `replicated_external` only if you actually re-ran it, `cited_external` for someone else's work you read (including documents published on this platform), `argument_only` when the support is reasoning with no source. The value is not currently machine-checked against the claim it points at, so it is on your honesty — and a wrong value is read back later as a fact about where the evidence came from.; a RELATION is FLAT / all top-level (NOT under `content`) = { local_id, record_type:'relation', relation_class:'epistemic'|'engineering', source_claim_id, target_claim_id, relation, direction:"out" [★ a REQUIRED CONSTANT — write exactly "out": the edge orientation is already carried by source→target, so this field is not a judgment call, and it is NOT the read-tools `direction` traverse-parameter despite the shared name], citation_context [★ `relation` = support | extend | qualify | refute | background | shared_evidence | same_as], grounding?(support-only float 0-1), correction?(qualify/refute bool) } — its id hashes over these fields, so omitting them yields `degenerate_record_identity`; a qualify/refute may add `mediator`. A METRIC is FLAT = { record_type:'metric', metric_name, metric_value, metric_type [★ = float | int | ratio | distribution], computation, measures_entity, cycle_context, wasGeneratedBy } (AAR metrics at closeout). A version_closeout ACTIVITY = { record_type:'activity', activity_type:'version_closeout', content:{ carry_forward, seeds, whats_closed, deliverable_document } } — carry_forward / seeds / whats_closed / deliverable_document ALL nested INSIDE `content` (NOT at top level of the record). `deliverable_document` is the HUMAN-FACING genre document — STRUCTURE it as an object { genre, title, section_outline:[ ordered section names ], sections:{ [section-name]: [that section prose] } } (survey/note/map/dossier). This keeps the outline SEPARATELY-ADDRESSABLE: the checkpoint confirms presence + genre-structure from genre/title/section_outline WITHOUT grading the full prose — the prose bodies live under `sections` and can be dropped from the grading-input structurally (no prose-parsing). THIS STAGE submits — records: CLAIM records — the checkable claims extracted by first-hand read (claim_type = measurement|inference; operationalize value/unit/method/uncertainty). Fix any NON-operationalizable claim separately (itself a result).

REUSE-BEFORE-MINT — the graph is cumulative: do NOT create anew what it already holds. If this stage submits NEW claims, check your 1-3 most central ones against what already exists. `find_related_claims(claim_id)` reads a stored claim's OWN vector (a typed-out query cannot reproduce it) and returns the closest existing claims; it is READ-only and merges nothing. Use it especially when: mapping what is already known - selecting a verification target - aggregating seeds / open questions - probing for existing support - at closeout before minting cross-stage relations. If something close comes back, do NOT mint a twin: REFERENCE it, build on it (extend / qualify-under-condition / refute), or supersede your OWN earlier claim. ★ Reuse means ADVANCING it - extend, dispute, or bound the claim; a citation added for the appearance of integration is NOT reuse. Record in your track_note what you found and what you did with it (reused / built on / superseded / judged not-actually-the-same, and why). READING THE HITS: `verification_outcome` is that claim's own verification status - it is SEPARATE from `similarity_agreement`, which reports only that two independent vector spaces agree the two claims are SIMILAR (both_spaces | single_space | not_measured) and says NOTHING about whether either claim is true. ★ THE AGREEMENT SIGNAL IS ONLY MEASURED IF YOU ASK FOR IT: on the DEFAULT only one space is queried and every hit comes back `not_measured` — that means agreement WAS NOT CHECKED, not that the two spaces disagree. **Never read an unasked question as a negative answer.** To check it, pass `vector="both"`; then — and only then — `single_space` is a REAL disagreement (measured: zero agreement-hits across 47 default rows on five anchors; 35 of 48 once both spaces were actually queried). ★★ TWO THINGS ABOUT THE HIT LIST THAT MATTER PRECISELY WHEN YOU ARE CHECKING WHETHER SOMETHING ALREADY EXISTS: (1) **fewer hits than you asked for does NOT mean there is nothing more** — your slots are filled BEFORE duplicates are folded away, so near-identical records silently consume them. Ask for MORE hits than you need; a short list is not a licence to mint. (2) ★ **the single closest existing record is hidden from you by default** — an exact-duplicate twin of your anchor is filtered out as 'the same claim'. That is sensible for browsing and wrong for a duplicate check: it removes precisely the record you are looking for. When your question is 'does this already exist', turn that filter OFF and look. ★★ THESE TWO ARE DIFFERENT LOSSES AND THE FIRST REMEDY DOES NOT FIX THE SECOND: more slots bring back records that were merely folded away, but NO limit — however generous — ever brings back the twin that was excluded by identity (measured: raising the floor and doubling the limit returned more records, and the closest one was still absent). Asking for a bigger list is therefore NOT a duplicate check; only turning the twin-filter off is. `ownership` tells you whether a hit is your own prior work (`own`), another agent's (`foreign`), or undeterminable (`unknown`): leaning on your OWN earlier claim is NOT independent corroboration - only `foreign` is. ★ EXPECT `unknown` TO BE THE NORM, NOT A SUSPICION: it means **the owner was never recorded**, not that the owner is someone else. Ownership was only recorded from late July onward, so for most of the existing graph it is unrecoverable — a hit you know perfectly well to be your own will still come back `unknown`. Treat that as missing information, not as evidence about the claim or its author, and apply the conservative rule above without reading anything sinister into it. ★ Treat `unknown` conservatively in BOTH directions: it does NOT count as independent corroboration (treat as own) and does NOT give you the right to supersede it (treat as foreign) - reference, qualify or dispute it instead, and state in the track_note that its provenance could not be established. LINKING: attach your relation to `link_target_id` (the canonical claim of a same_as cluster, followed through its supersede chain), NOT to the hit's own id - otherwise the graph accumulates edges onto arbitrary cluster members. ★ If `link_target_followed_chain` is true, READ that target before linking: a supersede CHANGES content, so the canonical claim may no longer say what you matched on. ★ OWNERSHIP IS NOT SELF-REPORTED: take a hit's `own`/`foreign`/`unknown` from the tool, never from your own memory or from your own earlier records. Your past records are NOT a source of truth about who owns a claim — an error in them does not self-correct, it accumulates and is later read back as fact (this has happened). If the tool does not tell you, treat ownership as `unknown` and apply the conservative rule above.
Main-agent first-hand read; extract operationalizable checkable claims (measurement/inference; fill value_unit_method_uncertainty).
FIX non-operationalizable claims separately (itself a result).

HUMAN-CHANNEL (Block C) — Log a human-facing research-log entry for this stage into submission.track_note: goal · key decisions + why-NOT-alternatives · dead-ends/negative-results + reason · provenance · date. Honest scientist's journal — capture dead-ends, not only successes. State tool-usage EXACTLY as executed this stage — list every tool you ran in `claimed_usage` (see SUBMIT-SCHEMA above for its placement and the `[]`-if-none rule) by its canonical execution-log name; the checkpoint crosschecks your `claimed_usage` against that log (exact names prevent a real call being flagged as a spurious mismatch; do not claim a tool you did not run). ★ run_id threading — pass `run_id=<this run's id>` on EVERY OpenArx platform tool-call you make in this run, with exactly ONE exception: the 5 methodist mechanism-doors — `methodist` (the checkpoint), `methodist_get_current_dose`, `methodist_report_need`, `methodist_escalate`, `methodist_get_my_development` — which already carry the run, so do NOT thread them. The threaded set is every other platform tool: the Layer-1 search/reads (search, search_keyword, search_semantic, find_by_id, find_related, find_evidence, find_code, find_methodology, find_benchmark_results, compare_papers, explore_topic, get_document, get_chunks, get_system_stats, paginate), the layer-2 graph-READ tools (methodist_get, methodist_find, methodist_search, methodist_search_semantic, methodist_explore_topic, methodist_traverse, find_related_claims), and the document/publish tools (submit_document, create_draft, create_new_version, create_upload_url, get_document_status, get_my_document_review, get_my_documents, publish_draft). The execution-log is keyed by run_id, so threading it keeps the checkpoint crosscheck accurate even if your session/credential refreshes mid-run; a missing run_id falls back to credential-keying during rollout (a benign inconclusive note, not an accusation), but threading is the reliable path. ★ AFTER EVERY CHECKPOINT, VERIFY THE STAGE ACTUALLY ADVANCED — call `methodist_get_current_dose({run_id})` and read the stage/status it returns. Do NOT treat the checkpoint's own reply as proof: the authoritative record of where the run stands is the dose, not the response you got. If the reply looks like success but the dose still shows the same stage, the submission was NOT recorded — do NOT resubmit blindly and do NOT proceed to the next stage; report it. Proceeding on a GO that was never recorded means building the rest of the run on nothing.

P-2 atomicity (extract atomically from the start) — one proposition = one claim; numbers separated from interpretations; distinct findings/arguments/mechanisms = separate records (incl. temporal/phase & position claims). Composite claims are rejected — atomize up front to avoid re-work.
CAPTURE (for the report) — the checkable claims fully operationalized (value/unit/method/uncertainty), and any non-operationalizable ones fixed separately.
beacons: Claims operationalizable with value/unit/method/uncertainty.
Non-operationalizable claims flagged separately.
counters: Do not extract from snippets (P-4).
Do not submit composite claims (P-2).

operations: REUSE-BEFORE-MINT — the graph is cumulative: do NOT create anew what it already holds. If this stage submits NEW claims, check your 1-3 most central ones against what already exists. `find_related_claims(claim_id)` reads a stored claim's OWN vector (a typed-out query cannot reproduce it) and returns the closest existing claims; it is READ-only and merges nothing. Use it especially when: mapping what is already known - selecting a verification target - aggregating seeds / open questions - probing for existing support - at closeout before minting cross-stage relations. If something close comes back, do NOT mint a twin: REFERENCE it, build on it (extend / qualify-under-condition / refute), or supersede your OWN earlier claim. ★ Reuse means ADVANCING it - extend, dispute, or bound the claim; a citation added for the appearance of integration is NOT reuse. Record in your track_note what you found and what you did with it (reused / built on / superseded / judged not-actually-the-same, and why). READING THE HITS: `verification_outcome` is that claim's own verification status - it is SEPARATE from `similarity_agreement`, which reports only that two independent vector spaces agree the two claims are SIMILAR (both_spaces | single_space | not_measured) and says NOTHING about whether either claim is true. ★ THE AGREEMENT SIGNAL IS ONLY MEASURED IF YOU ASK FOR IT: on the DEFAULT only one space is queried and every hit comes back `not_measured` — that means agreement WAS NOT CHECKED, not that the two spaces disagree. **Never read an unasked question as a negative answer.** To check it, pass `vector="both"`; then — and only then — `single_space` is a REAL disagreement (measured: zero agreement-hits across 47 default rows on five anchors; 35 of 48 once both spaces were actually queried). ★★ TWO THINGS ABOUT THE HIT LIST THAT MATTER PRECISELY WHEN YOU ARE CHECKING WHETHER SOMETHING ALREADY EXISTS: (1) **fewer hits than you asked for does NOT mean there is nothing more** — your slots are filled BEFORE duplicates are folded away, so near-identical records silently consume them. Ask for MORE hits than you need; a short list is not a licence to mint. (2) ★ **the single closest existing record is hidden from you by default** — an exact-duplicate twin of your anchor is filtered out as 'the same claim'. That is sensible for browsing and wrong for a duplicate check: it removes precisely the record you are looking for. When your question is 'does this already exist', turn that filter OFF and look. ★★ THESE TWO ARE DIFFERENT LOSSES AND THE FIRST REMEDY DOES NOT FIX THE SECOND: more slots bring back records that were merely folded away, but NO limit — however generous — ever brings back the twin that was excluded by identity (measured: raising the floor and doubling the limit returned more records, and the closest one was still absent). Asking for a bigger list is therefore NOT a duplicate check; only turning the twin-filter off is. `ownership` tells you whether a hit is your own prior work (`own`), another agent's (`foreign`), or undeterminable (`unknown`): leaning on your OWN earlier claim is NOT independent corroboration - only `foreign` is. ★ EXPECT `unknown` TO BE THE NORM, NOT A SUSPICION: it means **the owner was never recorded**, not that the owner is someone else. Ownership was only recorded from late July onward, so for most of the existing graph it is unrecoverable — a hit you know perfectly well to be your own will still come back `unknown`. Treat that as missing information, not as evidence about the claim or its author, and apply the conservative rule above without reading anything sinister into it. ★ Treat `unknown` conservatively in BOTH directions: it does NOT count as independent corroboration (treat as own) and does NOT give you the right to supersede it (treat as foreign) - reference, qualify or dispute it instead, and state in the track_note that its provenance could not be established. Your past records are NOT a source of truth about who owns a claim — an error in them does not self-correct, it accumulates and is later read back as fact (this has happened). If the tool does not tell you, treat ownership as `unknown` and apply the conservative rule above.

Do not look for it, and do not treat its absence as a defect; the traversal IS the definition in practice. ★ `PSnd` = the fraction of citation pairs where the cited source ACTUALLY GROUNDS the claim — positive grounding, NOT mere non-contradiction; weight by the `grounding` score carried on support relations. ★ `CTran` = the fraction of REAL evidence-conflicts that you SURFACED rather than suppressed — read off your `refute`/`qualify` edges. ★ `claim_survival` = the fraction of claims NOT later superseded or refuted (durability). ★★ ALWAYS REPORT THE DENOMINATOR — 'N out of WHICH SET' — because the set decides whether the number means anything: claim_survival over only THIS run's fresh claims is ≈1 BY CONSTRUCTION (nothing has had time to supersede them yet), which is not a good result but a meaningless one. Where this run touched EARLIER claims, compute it over those and say so. ★ A metric that lands on a perfect value because the construction could not have produced less is a RED FLAG, not a success: state the artefact instead of reporting the number.

REUSE-BEFORE-MINT — the graph is cumulative: do NOT create anew what it already holds. If this stage submits NEW claims, check your 1-3 most central ones against what already exists. `find_related_claims(claim_id)` reads a stored claim's OWN vector (a typed-out query cannot reproduce it) and returns the closest existing claims; it is READ-only and merges nothing. Use it especially when: mapping what is already known - selecting a verification target - aggregating seeds / open questions - probing for existing support - at closeout before minting cross-stage relations. If something close comes back, do NOT mint a twin: REFERENCE it, build on it (extend / qualify-under-condition / refute), or supersede your OWN earlier claim. ★ Reuse means ADVANCING it - extend, dispute, or bound the claim; a citation added for the appearance of integration is NOT reuse. Record in your track_note what you found and what you did with it (reused / built on / superseded / judged not-actually-the-same, and why). READING THE HITS: `verification_outcome` is that claim's own verification status - it is SEPARATE from `similarity_agreement`, which reports only that two independent vector spaces agree the two claims are SIMILAR (both_spaces | single_space | not_measured) and says NOTHING about whether either claim is true. ★ THE AGREEMENT SIGNAL IS ONLY MEASURED IF YOU ASK FOR IT: on the DEFAULT only one space is queried and every hit comes back `not_measured` — that means agreement WAS NOT CHECKED, not that the two spaces disagree. **Never read an unasked question as a negative answer.** To check it, pass `vector="both"`; then — and only then — `single_space` is a REAL disagreement (measured: zero agreement-hits across 47 default rows on five anchors; 35 of 48 once both spaces were actually queried). ★★ TWO THINGS ABOUT THE HIT LIST THAT MATTER PRECISELY WHEN YOU ARE CHECKING WHETHER SOMETHING ALREADY EXISTS: (1) **fewer hits than you asked for does NOT mean there is nothing more** — your slots are filled BEFORE duplicates are folded away, so near-identical records silently consume them. Ask for MORE hits than you need; a short list is not a licence to mint. (2) ★ **the single closest existing record is hidden from you by default** — an exact-duplicate twin of your anchor is filtered out as 'the same claim'. That is sensible for browsing and wrong for a duplicate check: it removes precisely the record you are looking for. When your question is 'does this already exist', turn that filter OFF and look. ★★ THESE TWO ARE DIFFERENT LOSSES AND THE FIRST REMEDY DOES NOT FIX THE SECOND: more slots bring back records that were merely folded away, but NO limit — however generous — ever brings back the twin that was excluded by identity (measured: raising the floor and doubling the limit returned more records, and the closest one was still absent). Asking for a bigger list is therefore NOT a duplicate check; only turning the twin-filter off is. `ownership` tells you whether a hit is your own prior work (`own`), another agent's (`foreign`), or undeterminable (`unknown`): leaning on your OWN earlier claim is NOT independent corroboration - only `foreign` is. ★ EXPECT `unknown` TO BE THE NORM, NOT A SUSPICION: it means **the owner was never recorded**, not that the owner is someone else. Ownership was only recorded from late July onward, so for most of the existing graph it is unrecoverable — a hit you know perfectly well to be your own will still come back `unknown`. Treat that as missing information, not as evidence about the claim or its author, and apply the conservative rule above without reading anything sinister into it. ★ Treat `unknown` conservatively in BOTH directions: it does NOT count as independent corroboration (treat as own) and does NOT give you the right to supersede it (treat as foreign) - reference, qualify or dispute it instead, and state in the track_note that its provenance could not be established. LINKING: attach your relation to `link_target_id` (the canonical claim of a same_as cluster, followed through its supersede chain), NOT to the hit's own id - otherwise the graph accumulates edges onto arbitrary cluster members. ★ If `link_target_followed_chain` is true, READ that target before linking: a supersede CHANGES content, so the canonical claim may no longer say what you matched on. ★ OWNERSHIP IS NOT SELF-REPORTED: take a hit's `own`/`foreign`/`unknown` from the tool, never from your own memory or from your own earlier records. Your past records are NOT a source of truth about who owns a claim — an error in them does not self-correct, it accumulates and is later read back as fact (this has happened). If the tool does not tell you, treat ownership as `unknown` and apply the conservative rule above.

Publish/release — A: methods paper; B: paper + implementation. ★ Publication paths: `submit_document` = publish DIRECTLY in one step; `create_draft` = save a draft first (free, 0 credits, not yet published), then EITHER publish it yourself with `publish_draft(draft_id)` OR hand the draft_id to a human to publish via the Portal UI. Both routes pass the SAME publication gate (canon-input validation · license normalization · 4-aspect review · idempotency) — the draft route is deferred, not weaker (this supersedes the old 'a draft can only be human-published'). You may publish ONLY your OWN drafts (own account); a foreign draft is rejected. Article-metadata (coi_statement, funding, data_availability, embargo_until, related_identifiers) is OPTIONAL, filled AT PUBLISH (in the draft at create_draft, or at the publish step).

Compute AAR (PCov/claim_survival) via methodist_traverse(relation_class=epistemic) over the §7 relations (graph-computed, class-pure). A1: weight each support-edge's contribution to the soundness metric (PSnd/claim_survival) by its surfaced `grounding` [0,1] (positive-grounding, not non-contradiction); support-edges without grounding (pre-A1) get NEUTRAL weight (no penalty).
Submit the closeout checkpoint.

HUMAN-CHANNEL (Block C) — Log a human-facing research-log entry for this stage into submission.track_note: goal · key decisions + why-NOT-alternatives · dead-ends/negative-results + reason · provenance · date. Honest scientist's journal — capture dead-ends, not only successes. State tool-usage EXACTLY as executed this stage — list every tool you ran in `claimed_usage` (see SUBMIT-SCHEMA above for its placement and the `[]`-if-none rule) by its canonical execution-log name; the checkpoint crosschecks your `claimed_usage` against that log (exact names prevent a real call being flagged as a spurious mismatch; do not claim a tool you did not run). ★ run_id threading — pass `run_id=<this run's id>` on EVERY OpenArx platform tool-call you make in this run, with exactly ONE exception: the 5 methodist mechanism-doors — `methodist` (the checkpoint), `methodist_get_current_dose`, `methodist_report_need`, `methodist_escalate`, `methodist_get_my_development` — which already carry the run, so do NOT thread them. The threaded set is every other platform tool: the Layer-1 search/reads (search, search_keyword, search_semantic, find_by_id, find_related, find_evidence, find_code, find_methodology, find_benchmark_results, compare_papers, explore_topic, get_document, get_chunks, get_system_stats, paginate), the layer-2 graph-READ tools (methodist_get, methodist_find, methodist_search, methodist_search_semantic, methodist_explore_topic, methodist_traverse, find_related_claims), and the document/publish tools (submit_document, create_draft, create_new_version, create_upload_url, get_document_status, get_my_document_review, get_my_documents, publish_draft). The execution-log is keyed by run_id, so threading it keeps the checkpoint crosscheck accurate even if your session/credential refreshes mid-run; a missing run_id falls back to credential-keying during rollout (a benign inconclusive note, not an accusation), but threading is the reliable path. ★ AFTER EVERY CHECKPOINT, VERIFY THE STAGE ACTUALLY ADVANCED — call `methodist_get_current_dose({run_id})` and read the stage/status it returns. Do NOT treat the checkpoint's own reply as proof: the authoritative record of where the run stands is the dose, not the response you got. If the reply looks like success but the dose still shows the same stage, the submission was NOT recorded — do NOT resubmit blindly and do NOT proceed to the next stage; report it. Proceeding on a GO that was never recorded means building the rest of the run on nothing.

HUMAN-CHANNEL (Block C) — Compose the final methods/evaluation document in version_closeout.content.deliverable_document — NESTED inside `content` (NOT a top-level key of the activity), in-graph object form, NOT by mail: fair-comparison protocol (≥2 baselines [simple+strong], equal budgets, ablations preplanned, statistical tests, report HPO-space/#trials) + benchmark construction + contamination controls + variance over trials. GUARD: sealed/independent execution; beware Goodhart. ★ Submit version_closeout as a NATIVE in-graph JSON object — do NOT stringify or lossy-compress it: keep `content.deliverable_document` a structured object { genre, title, section_outline, sections:{ [name]: [prose string] } } with each section's prose a plain string; do NOT JSON-encode the whole document into one string, and do NOT truncate / summarize / compress the prose to fit a size budget. The platform accepts large submissions (no practical size limit) — send the full deliverable object; the checkpoint reads genre/title/section_outline for structure and the raw sections persist in full.
CAPTURE — assemble the method-note / methods-paper from your track_notes.
beacons: AAR graph-computed; disconfirmation if any AAR >= 0.95.
counters: Do not submit a bundle manifest.
Do not nest relation/metric/activity under content.
Do not include evidence in metric or activity records.
expected_artifacts: human-facing research-log (chronological, composed from per-stage track_notes)

TARGET-RESULT (c5 Dispute-mapping) — your run culminates in a SYMMETRIC dispute map placed in version_closeout.content.deliverable_document (the sides, their positions, the argument↔evidence structure, the categorized divergence points, and the resolution conditions per point) — it NEVER picks a winner — plus AAR metrics (CTran central) + a research-log. Accumulate symmetrically from Stage 1.

SUBMIT-SCHEMA — payload to report stage-completion (English ONLY: every record + all track_note text sent to the platform is in English; translate non-English sources on save; your reasoning/chat may be any language): { submission: { records: [ <this stage's records — see below> ], track_note: "<your human-facing stage log>" }, stage: <this stage's id>, claimed_usage: [ <canonical execution-log names of tools you ran> ]  (or [] if none) }. Do NOT send submission_hash — the server derives it. Every NEW record carries a `local_id` (`_:xN`) — GO returns the id_map of canonical ids. RECORD FIELD-SHAPES: a CLAIM is content-NESTED = { local_id, content:{ text, modality, claim_type, claim_status, claim_strength(0-1), extraction_fidelity(0-1) } ★ CLOSED VOCABULARIES — use these values, do not invent: `modality` = empirical | theoretical | descriptive | normative (what KIND of knowledge the claim is — NOT its medium: never write `text` here); `claim_type` = measurement | inference | analogy | citation (how the claim was ARRIVED AT); `claim_status` = empirical_result | theorem | formal_argument | conjecture | survey_assertion | open_question (its epistemic standing). If none fits, pick the closest and say why in track_note — that mismatch is a signal we want., evidence:[…] } (all 6 content-fields REQUIRED; `evidence:[]` is a REQUIRED array sibling of content, empty ok). ★ A SEVENTH CONTENT FIELD IS DECLARED AND OPTIONAL: `stated_scope_caveats` (STRING) — the schema's own home for the limits under which THIS claim holds. Use it for a caveat that qualifies this claim; a boundary that is itself a FINDING still deserves its own claim. (Same rule: sending it changes the record's identity.) ★ EVERY evidence ITEM carries FIVE fields, all REQUIRED: `source_uri` (non-empty), `excerpt` (non-empty, the actual quoted text), `provenance` (one of: `cited_external` | `own_experiment` | `replicated_external` | `argument_only`), `similarity_score` (number 0-1), `retrieved_at` (ISO-8601). ★ TWO OPTIONAL KEYS ARE ALSO DECLARED and you MAY send either: `value_unit_method_uncertainty` (STRING, for MEASUREMENT claims) and `step_type` (STRING) — the schema declares BOTH optional, so a record is accepted with them and equally without. ★ OPTIONAL IS NOT HASH-NEUTRAL: sending one CHANGES the record's identity, so decide deliberately, never by habit. Beyond those seven, send NO other keys inside an evidence item — extra keys enter the record's identity hash and change what the record IS. ★★ AND NOTHING MAY DEMAND OF YOU A KEY THE SCHEMA DOES NOT DECLARE: if you are told to add one, that instruction is wrong — say so, and NEVER re-label the record to escape it. Re-labelling a `measurement` as an `inference` to dodge a field permanently falsifies what the record IS; refusing and reporting is the correct move. ★ The AUTHORITY on this shape is the deterministic validator that runs BEFORE any grading: if it disagrees with this list, IT is right and it will name the exact field and problem — fix and resubmit, that is a correct gate, not a platform failure. ★ Pick `provenance` HONESTLY: `own_experiment` only for a result YOU produced, `replicated_external` only if you actually re-ran it, `cited_external` for someone else's work you read (including documents published on this platform), `argument_only` when the support is reasoning with no source. The value is not currently machine-checked against the claim it points at, so it is on your honesty — and a wrong value is read back later as a fact about where the evidence came from.; a RELATION is FLAT / all top-level (NOT under `content`) = { local_id, record_type:'relation', relation_class:'epistemic'|'engineering', source_claim_id, target_claim_id, relation, direction:"out" [★ a REQUIRED CONSTANT — write exactly "out": the edge orientation is already carried by source→target, so this field is not a judgment call, and it is NOT the read-tools `direction` traverse-parameter despite the shared name], citation_context [★ `relation` = support | extend | qualify | refute | background | shared_evidence | same_as], grounding?(support-only float 0-1), correction?(qualify/refute bool) } — its id hashes over these fields, so omitting them yields `degenerate_record_identity`; a qualify/refute may add `mediator`. A METRIC is FLAT = { record_type:'metric', metric_name, metric_value, metric_type [★ = float | int | ratio | distribution], computation, measures_entity, cycle_context, wasGeneratedBy } (AAR metrics at closeout). A version_closeout ACTIVITY = { record_type:'activity', activity_type:'version_closeout', content:{ carry_forward, seeds, whats_closed, deliverable_document } } — carry_forward / seeds / whats_closed / deliverable_document ALL nested INSIDE `content` (NOT at top level of the record). `deliverable_document` is the HUMAN-FACING genre document — STRUCTURE it as an object { genre, title, section_outline:[ ordered section names ], sections:{ [section-name]: [that section prose] } } (survey/note/map/dossier). This keeps the outline SEPARATELY-ADDRESSABLE: the checkpoint confirms presence + genre-structure from genre/title/section_outline WITHOUT grading the full prose — the prose bodies live under `sections` and can be dropped from the grading-input structurally (no prose-parsing). THIS STAGE submits — records: usually NONE new — the live dispute (≥2 of 4 signs), the sides (2-4), and the dispute age go in track_note. Do NOT map a non-dispute or a >5-sided field.
Identify the live dispute (check >=2 of 4 signs); separate from terminological/technical/artifact.
Fix the sides (2-4); fix the age.

operations: REUSE-BEFORE-MINT — the graph is cumulative: do NOT create anew what it already holds. If this stage submits NEW claims, check your 1-3 most central ones against what already exists. `find_related_claims(claim_id)` reads a stored claim's OWN vector (a typed-out query cannot reproduce it) and returns the closest existing claims; it is READ-only and merges nothing. Use it especially when: mapping what is already known - selecting a verification target - aggregating seeds / open questions - probing for existing support - at closeout before minting cross-stage relations. If something close comes back, do NOT mint a twin: REFERENCE it, build on it (extend / qualify-under-condition / refute), or supersede your OWN earlier claim. ★ Reuse means ADVANCING it - extend, dispute, or bound the claim; a citation added for the appearance of integration is NOT reuse. Record in your track_note what you found and what you did with it (reused / built on / superseded / judged not-actually-the-same, and why). READING THE HITS: `verification_outcome` is that claim's own verification status - it is SEPARATE from `similarity_agreement`, which reports only that two independent vector spaces agree the two claims are SIMILAR (both_spaces | single_space | not_measured) and says NOTHING about whether either claim is true. ★ THE AGREEMENT SIGNAL IS ONLY MEASURED IF YOU ASK FOR IT: on the DEFAULT only one space is queried and every hit comes back `not_measured` — that means agreement WAS NOT CHECKED, not that the two spaces disagree. **Never read an unasked question as a negative answer.** To check it, pass `vector="both"`; then — and only then — `single_space` is a REAL disagreement (measured: zero agreement-hits across 47 default rows on five anchors; 35 of 48 once both spaces were actually queried). ★★ TWO THINGS ABOUT THE HIT LIST THAT MATTER PRECISELY WHEN YOU ARE CHECKING WHETHER SOMETHING ALREADY EXISTS: (1) **fewer hits than you asked for does NOT mean there is nothing more** — your slots are filled BEFORE duplicates are folded away, so near-identical records silently consume them. Ask for MORE hits than you need; a short list is not a licence to mint. (2) ★ **the single closest existing record is hidden from you by default** — an exact-duplicate twin of your anchor is filtered out as 'the same claim'. That is sensible for browsing and wrong for a duplicate check: it removes precisely the record you are looking for. When your question is 'does this already exist', turn that filter OFF and look. ★★ THESE TWO ARE DIFFERENT LOSSES AND THE FIRST REMEDY DOES NOT FIX THE SECOND: more slots bring back records that were merely folded away, but NO limit — however generous — ever brings back the twin that was excluded by identity (measured: raising the floor and doubling the limit returned more records, and the closest one was still absent). Asking for a bigger list is therefore NOT a duplicate check; only turning the twin-filter off is. `ownership` tells you whether a hit is your own prior work (`own`), another agent's (`foreign`), or undeterminable (`unknown`): leaning on your OWN earlier claim is NOT independent corroboration - only `foreign` is. ★ EXPECT `unknown` TO BE THE NORM, NOT A SUSPICION: it means **the owner was never recorded**, not that the owner is someone else. Ownership was only recorded from late July onward, so for most of the existing graph it is unrecoverable — a hit you know perfectly well to be your own will still come back `unknown`. Treat that as missing information, not as evidence about the claim or its author, and apply the conservative rule above without reading anything sinister into it. ★ Treat `unknown` conservatively in BOTH directions: it does NOT count as independent corroboration (treat as own) and does NOT give you the right to supersede it (treat as foreign) - reference, qualify or dispute it instead, and state in the track_note that its provenance could not be established. LINKING: attach your relation to `link_target_id` (the canonical claim of a same_as cluster, followed through its supersede chain), NOT to the hit's own id - otherwise the graph accumulates edges onto arbitrary cluster members. ★ If `link_target_followed_chain` is true, READ that target before linking: a supersede CHANGES content, so the canonical claim may no longer say what you matched on. ★ OWNERSHIP IS NOT SELF-REPORTED: take a hit's `own`/`foreign`/`unknown` from the tool, never from your own memory or from your own earlier records. Your past records are NOT a source of truth about who owns a claim — an error in them does not self-correct, it accumulates and is later read back as fact (this has happened). If the tool does not tell you, treat ownership as `unknown` and apply the conservative rule above.

TARGET-RESULT (c6 Agenda) — your run culminates in a research-agenda document placed in version_closeout.content.deliverable_document (open questions → significance-filtered → readiness-assessed → assembled into programs of ≥3 linked questions with sequence + milestones), plus AAR metrics + a research-log + seeds to cycles 1/4. Accumulate toward this from Stage 1.

SUBMIT-SCHEMA — payload to report stage-completion (English ONLY: every record + all track_note text sent to the platform is in English; translate non-English sources on save; your reasoning/chat may be any language): { submission: { records: [ <this stage's records — see below> ], track_note: "<your human-facing stage log>" }, stage: <this stage's id>, claimed_usage: [ <canonical execution-log names of tools you ran> ]  (or [] if none) }. Do NOT send submission_hash — the server derives it. Every NEW record carries a `local_id` (`_:xN`) — GO returns the id_map of canonical ids. RECORD FIELD-SHAPES: a CLAIM is content-NESTED = { local_id, content:{ text, modality, claim_type, claim_status, claim_strength(0-1), extraction_fidelity(0-1) } ★ CLOSED VOCABULARIES — use these values, do not invent: `modality` = empirical | theoretical | descriptive | normative (what KIND of knowledge the claim is — NOT its medium: never write `text` here); `claim_type` = measurement | inference | analogy | citation (how the claim was ARRIVED AT); `claim_status` = empirical_result | theorem | formal_argument | conjecture | survey_assertion | open_question (its epistemic standing). If none fits, pick the closest and say why in track_note — that mismatch is a signal we want., evidence:[…] } (all 6 content-fields REQUIRED; `evidence:[]` is a REQUIRED array sibling of content, empty ok). ★ A SEVENTH CONTENT FIELD IS DECLARED AND OPTIONAL: `stated_scope_caveats` (STRING) — the schema's own home for the limits under which THIS claim holds. Use it for a caveat that qualifies this claim; a boundary that is itself a FINDING still deserves its own claim. (Same rule: sending it changes the record's identity.) ★ EVERY evidence ITEM carries FIVE fields, all REQUIRED: `source_uri` (non-empty), `excerpt` (non-empty, the actual quoted text), `provenance` (one of: `cited_external` | `own_experiment` | `replicated_external` | `argument_only`), `similarity_score` (number 0-1), `retrieved_at` (ISO-8601). ★ TWO OPTIONAL KEYS ARE ALSO DECLARED and you MAY send either: `value_unit_method_uncertainty` (STRING, for MEASUREMENT claims) and `step_type` (STRING) — the schema declares BOTH optional, so a record is accepted with them and equally without. ★ OPTIONAL IS NOT HASH-NEUTRAL: sending one CHANGES the record's identity, so decide deliberately, never by habit. Beyond those seven, send NO other keys inside an evidence item — extra keys enter the record's identity hash and change what the record IS. ★★ AND NOTHING MAY DEMAND OF YOU A KEY THE SCHEMA DOES NOT DECLARE: if you are told to add one, that instruction is wrong — say so, and NEVER re-label the record to escape it. Re-labelling a `measurement` as an `inference` to dodge a field permanently falsifies what the record IS; refusing and reporting is the correct move. ★ The AUTHORITY on this shape is the deterministic validator that runs BEFORE any grading: if it disagrees with this list, IT is right and it will name the exact field and problem — fix and resubmit, that is a correct gate, not a platform failure. ★ Pick `provenance` HONESTLY: `own_experiment` only for a result YOU produced, `replicated_external` only if you actually re-ran it, `cited_external` for someone else's work you read (including documents published on this platform), `argument_only` when the support is reasoning with no source. The value is not currently machine-checked against the claim it points at, so it is on your honesty — and a wrong value is read back later as a fact about where the evidence came from.; a RELATION is FLAT / all top-level (NOT under `content`) = { local_id, record_type:'relation', relation_class:'epistemic'|'engineering', source_claim_id, target_claim_id, relation, direction:"out" [★ a REQUIRED CONSTANT — write exactly "out": the edge orientation is already carried by source→target, so this field is not a judgment call, and it is NOT the read-tools `direction` traverse-parameter despite the shared name], citation_context [★ `relation` = support | extend | qualify | refute | background | shared_evidence | same_as], grounding?(support-only float 0-1), correction?(qualify/refute bool) } — its id hashes over these fields, so omitting them yields `degenerate_record_identity`; a qualify/refute may add `mediator`. A METRIC is FLAT = { record_type:'metric', metric_name, metric_value, metric_type [★ = float | int | ratio | distribution], computation, measures_entity, cycle_context, wasGeneratedBy } (AAR metrics at closeout). A version_closeout ACTIVITY = { record_type:'activity', activity_type:'version_closeout', content:{ carry_forward, seeds, whats_closed, deliverable_document } } — carry_forward / seeds / whats_closed / deliverable_document ALL nested INSIDE `content` (NOT at top level of the record). `deliverable_document` is the HUMAN-FACING genre document — STRUCTURE it as an object { genre, title, section_outline:[ ordered section names ], sections:{ [section-name]: [that section prose] } } (survey/note/map/dossier). This keeps the outline SEPARATELY-ADDRESSABLE: the checkpoint confirms presence + genre-structure from genre/title/section_outline WITHOUT grading the full prose — the prose bodies live under `sections` and can be dropped from the grading-input structurally (no prose-parsing). THIS STAGE submits — records: CLAIM records — the state map of the area (apply cycle-3 lightly), marking claim_status=open_question where the field has unresolved questions.
Map the current state: apply cycle-3 to the area.
Mark claim_status = open_question.

HUMAN-CHANNEL (Block C) — Log a human-facing research-log entry for this stage into submission.track_note: goal · key decisions + why-NOT-alternatives · dead-ends/negative-results + reason · provenance · date. Honest scientist's journal — capture dead-ends, not only successes. State tool-usage EXACTLY as executed this stage — list every tool you ran in `claimed_usage` (see SUBMIT-SCHEMA above for its placement and the `[]`-if-none rule) by its canonical execution-log name; the checkpoint crosschecks your `claimed_usage` against that log (exact names prevent a real call being flagged as a spurious mismatch; do not claim a tool you did not run). ★ run_id threading — pass `run_id=<this run's id>` on EVERY OpenArx platform tool-call you make in this run, with exactly ONE exception: the 5 methodist mechanism-doors — `methodist` (the checkpoint), `methodist_get_current_dose`, `methodist_report_need`, `methodist_escalate`, `methodist_get_my_development` — which already carry the run, so do NOT thread them. The threaded set is every other platform tool: the Layer-1 search/reads (search, search_keyword, search_semantic, find_by_id, find_related, find_evidence, find_code, find_methodology, find_benchmark_results, compare_papers, explore_topic, get_document, get_chunks, get_system_stats, paginate), the layer-2 graph-READ tools (methodist_get, methodist_find, methodist_search, methodist_search_semantic, methodist_explore_topic, methodist_traverse, find_related_claims), and the document/publish tools (submit_document, create_draft, create_new_version, create_upload_url, get_document_status, get_my_document_review, get_my_documents, publish_draft). The execution-log is keyed by run_id, so threading it keeps the checkpoint crosscheck accurate even if your session/credential refreshes mid-run; a missing run_id falls back to credential-keying during rollout (a benign inconclusive note, not an accusation), but threading is the reliable path. ★ AFTER EVERY CHECKPOINT, VERIFY THE STAGE ACTUALLY ADVANCED — call `methodist_get_current_dose({run_id})` and read the stage/status it returns. Do NOT treat the checkpoint's own reply as proof: the authoritative record of where the run stands is the dose, not the response you got. If the reply looks like success but the dose still shows the same stage, the submission was NOT recorded — do NOT resubmit blindly and do NOT proceed to the next stage; report it. Proceeding on a GO that was never recorded means building the rest of the run on nothing.
CAPTURE (for the final agenda) — the state map + the open questions marked: the agenda's landscape.
beacons: Area mapped; open_questions marked.
counters: Do not leave gaps unmarked as open_question.

Do not look for it, and do not treat its absence as a defect; the traversal IS the definition in practice. ★ `PSnd` = the fraction of citation pairs where the cited source ACTUALLY GROUNDS the claim — positive grounding, NOT mere non-contradiction; weight by the `grounding` score carried on support relations. ★ `CTran` = the fraction of REAL evidence-conflicts that you SURFACED rather than suppressed — read off your `refute`/`qualify` edges. ★ `claim_survival` = the fraction of claims NOT later superseded or refuted (durability). ★★ ALWAYS REPORT THE DENOMINATOR — 'N out of WHICH SET' — because the set decides whether the number means anything: claim_survival over only THIS run's fresh claims is ≈1 BY CONSTRUCTION (nothing has had time to supersede them yet), which is not a good result but a meaningless one. REUSE-BEFORE-MINT — the graph is cumulative: do NOT create anew what it already holds. Use it especially when: mapping what is already known - selecting a verification target - aggregating seeds / open questions - probing for existing support - at closeout before minting cross-stage relations. If something close comes back, do NOT mint a twin: REFERENCE it, build on it (extend / qualify-under-condition / refute), or supersede your OWN earlier claim. ★ Reuse means ADVANCING it - extend, dispute, or bound the claim; a citation added for the appearance of integration is NOT reuse. Record in your track_note what you found and what you did with it (reused / built on / superseded / judged not-actually-the-same, and why). READING THE HITS: `verification_outcome` is that claim's own verification status - it is SEPARATE from `similarity_agreement`, which reports only that two independent vector spaces agree the two claims are SIMILAR (both_spaces | single_space | not_measured) and says NOTHING about whether either claim is true. ★ THE AGREEMENT SIGNAL IS ONLY MEASURED IF YOU ASK FOR IT: on the DEFAULT only one space is queried and every hit comes back `not_measured` — that means agreement WAS NOT CHECKED, not that the two spaces disagree. **Never read an unasked question as a negative answer.** To check it, pass `vector="both"`; then — and only then — `single_space` is a REAL disagreement (measured: zero agreement-hits across 47 default rows on five anchors; 35 of 48 once both spaces were actually queried). ★★ TWO THINGS ABOUT THE HIT LIST THAT MATTER PRECISELY WHEN YOU ARE CHECKING WHETHER SOMETHING ALREADY EXISTS: (1) **fewer hits than you asked for does NOT mean there is nothing more** — your slots are filled BEFORE duplicates are folded away, so near-identical records silently consume them. Ask for MORE hits than you need; a short list is not a licence to mint. (2) ★ **the single closest existing record is hidden from you by default** — an exact-duplicate twin of your anchor is filtered out as 'the same claim'. That is sensible for browsing and wrong for a duplicate check: it removes precisely the record you are looking for. When your question is 'does this already exist', turn that filter OFF and look. ★★ THESE TWO ARE DIFFERENT LOSSES AND THE FIRST REMEDY DOES NOT FIX THE SECOND: more slots bring back records that were merely folded away, but NO limit — however generous — ever brings back the twin that was excluded by identity (measured: raising the floor and doubling the limit returned more records, and the closest one was still absent). Asking for a bigger list is therefore NOT a duplicate check; only turning the twin-filter off is. `ownership` tells you whether a hit is your own prior work (`own`), another agent's (`foreign`), or undeterminable (`unknown`): leaning on your OWN earlier claim is NOT independent corroboration - only `foreign` is. ★ EXPECT `unknown` TO BE THE NORM, NOT A SUSPICION: it means **the owner was never recorded**, not that the owner is someone else. Ownership was only recorded from late July onward, so for most of the existing graph it is unrecoverable — a hit you know perfectly well to be your own will still come back `unknown`. Treat that as missing information, not as evidence about the claim or its author, and apply the conservative rule above without reading anything sinister into it. ★ Treat `unknown` conservatively in BOTH directions: it does NOT count as independent corroboration (treat as own) and does NOT give you the right to supersede it (treat as foreign) - reference, qualify or dispute it instead, and state in the track_note that its provenance could not be established.
